problems.title: Pair Sum in a Sorted List
problems.statement:
You get a list of integers `nums` sorted from smallest to largest, and a number `target`.
Find the two different positions whose values add up to `target` and return them as `[i, j]` with `i < j`.

Exactly one such pair exists.
hints: Because the list is sorted, a sum that is too small can only grow by moving the left side right.
Start one pointer at each end.

approaches.name: Two Pointers
approaches.idea:
Put one pointer, L, on the smallest number and another, R, on the largest.

If their sum is too small, the only way to grow it is to move L to the right. If it is too big, move R to the left. Each step throws away one number that can never be part of the answer.

code.name: solution.py
Solution.java

approaches.why: Each step moves one pointer inward, so we take at most n steps and only store two indexes.

problems.title: Reverse a Linked List
problems.statement: Given the `head` of a singly linked list, reverse the list so the last node becomes the first, and return the new head.
hints: Walk the list once, flipping each arrow to point backwards.
Keep a pointer to the previous node.

approaches.name: Two Pointers (prev & cur)
approaches.idea:
Use two pointers: `prev` starts empty and `cur` starts at the head.

At each node, remember the next node, flip `cur.next` to point back at `prev`, then slide both pointers one step forward. When `cur` falls off the end, `prev` is the new head.

code.name: solution.py
code.src:
def reverse_list(head):
    prev, cur = None, head
    while cur:
        nxt = cur.next
        cur.next = prev
        prev, cur = cur, nxt
    return prev

problems.title: Longest Stretch Without Repeats
problems.statement: Given a string `s`, return the length of the longest contiguous piece of `s` in which no character appears twice.

examples.why: "abc" has no repeats and nothing longer works.

hints: Keep a window with no repeats.
When a repeat enters, jump the left edge past the previous copy.

approaches.name: Sliding Window
approaches.idea:
Keep a window from L to R that never contains a repeat, and remember the last index where each character was seen.

When the new character at R was already seen inside the window, jump L just past that earlier copy. The window is valid again, so we update the best length.

code.name: solution.py
Solution.java

approaches.why: R visits every character once and L only moves forward, so the work is linear. The map holds at most one entry per distinct character, k.
